get.description:
List the workspaces the authenticated user can view.

This is a discovery endpoint, with two consequences for how it is called:

- Authentication must be an OAuth 2.0 bearer token. API key authentication
  is not accepted, because API-key requests require a workspace ID and
  this is a pre-workspace discovery route.
- The `x-air-workspace-id` header is not required, since the purpose of the
  call is to discover which workspaces are available before any
  workspace-scoped call is made.

Results are filtered to workspaces the authenticated principal has
permission to view.

Requires the `workspace.read` OAuth scope.

get.description:
List the share links for an asset.

An asset can have one link that follows its current version and one link per pinned version. Older links created from inside a board are listed too, so an asset can have more than one link that follows the current version. Tell them apart by `id` and `createdAt`.

Links that follow the current version come first, then pinned links from the newest version to the oldest. If you can't view all of the asset's versions, only links for its current version are returned.

Disabled links are included with `active: false`. The password is never returned; `hasPassword` says whether one is set.

Requires the `share_links.read` and `assets.read` OAuth scopes.

followsDefaultVersion.description: Create a link that always shows the asset's current version. Only `true` is accepted.

versionId.description: Pin the link to this version of the asset. Don't send `followsDefaultVersion` with it.

400.description: Invalid request body: neither or both of `followsDefaultVersion` and `versionId`, `followsDefaultVersion` other than `true`, a `null` value where it is not allowed, or an `expiresAt` that is not in the future

403.description: You do not have permission to create share links for this asset, or the link would let visitors do something you can't, such as download the original

404.description: Asset not found, or `Version not found` when `versionId` is not a version of this asset

409.description: The asset already has a link that follows its current version, or a link pinned to this version (`SHARE_LINK_ALREADY_EXISTS`)

422.description: The request turns on a share link setting your workspace's plan does not include (`ADDON_DISABLED`). `extra.addonKey` is `shareLinks` and `extra.settings` lists them.

post.description:
Create a share link for an asset.

Use `followsDefaultVersion: true` for a link that always shows the asset's current version, or `versionId` to pin the link to one version.

Any field not listed in the request body is ignored. Settings you leave out follow your workspace's share link defaults. A new link is active unless you send `active: false`.

`password`, `expiresAt`, `requireAccount`, `comments` and `customFields` depend on your workspace's plan; see the request body for what returns `422`.

Returns `409 Conflict` if the asset already has a link of the same kind, even a disabled one. A version has one pinned link whatever its `showAllVersions` setting. Older links created from inside a board don't count, so the asset can end up with more than one link that follows its current version. Use `GET /v1/assets/{assetId}/share-links` to find the existing link, and `PATCH` to change it.

Returns `403` if the link's settings, including the ones taken from your workspace defaults, would let visitors do something you can't do yourself.

Requires the `share_links.write` and `assets.read` OAuth scopes.

patch.description:
Change the settings of one of an asset's share links.

Any field not listed in the request body is ignored. Only the settings you send change. Everything else on the link, including its password, stays as it is. Send `password: null` or `expiresAt: null` to remove them.

`password`, `expiresAt`, `requireAccount`, `comments` and `customFields` depend on your workspace's plan; see the request body for what returns `422`.

Returns `403` if the link lets visitors do something you can't do yourself, even when you only change `active`.

On a link pinned to a version, `showAllVersions` keeps the link pinned to the same version and changes only whether visitors can browse the asset's other versions.

Returns an empty body on success. Use `GET /v1/assets/{assetId}/share-links` to read the link's settings.

Requires the `share_links.write` and `assets.read` OAuth scopes.

get.description:
List discussions on an asset or on the assets currently in a board.

One of `assetId` or `boardId` is required. They cannot be combined.
Each discussion includes at most 10 comments, oldest first. When
`comments.pagination.hasMore` is true, pass `comments.pagination.cursor`
to `GET /v1/discussions/{discussionId}/comments`.

**Sort.** Default is `sortBy=lastCommentedAt&sortDirection=desc`. Pages
don't overlap. With the default `lastCommentedAt` sort, a reply between
pages can move a discussion, so it may repeat or be skipped. For a
stable walk, use `sortBy=createdAt&sortDirection=asc`: `createdAt` is
the first comment and does not move, and a discussion started while
you page sorts after the cursor and still shows up. With
`sortDirection=desc`, a discussion started after your first page sorts
before the cursor and is missed until you list from the beginning.

**Boards.** In a workspace that does not scope comments to boards,
`?boardId=` returns every discussion on assets currently on that board,
including discussions started on another board. Discussions that are
visible on those assets but were not returned are listed with
`?assetId=` per asset. In a workspace that scopes comments to boards,
`?boardId=` returns only discussions stored on that board, and
`?assetId=` without `boardId` returns discussions with no board. That
no-board list is empty unless the caller has `asset.canViewDiscussions`
on both the asset and the workspace.

`boardId` on a discussion is present only when the stored board is
still active and the caller can view it. A trashed stored board is
omitted: the discussion stays on an asset list in an unscoped
workspace, and it is not part of the no-board asset list in a scoped
workspace. Permanently deleting a board deletes discussions created in
it, including ones that were visible on the asset in an unscoped
workspace.

Comment `body` is user-generated. Escape it before rendering HTML.
`mentions` is parsed from the stored text. `id` there is the same
account id as `author.id` for a workspace account and as `id` on
`GET /v1/members`.

Requires the `comments.read` OAuth scope.

400.description: Invalid body, mentions, version, or annotation

403.description: You cannot manage discussions on this asset. In a workspace that scopes comments to boards, you also need that permission at the workspace level.

404.description: Asset or version not found

post.description:
Start a discussion on an asset version.

`assetVersionId` is required. There is no default to the current
version. The current version is `coverVersion.id` on
`GET /v1/assets/{assetId}`.

The body has no board. A `boardId` in the body is ignored. In a
workspace that scopes comments to boards, a discussion with no board
needs `asset.canManageDiscussions` at the workspace level, so a board
guest gets 403 here even when they can comment in their board.

`body` is plain text, 1 to 500 characters counted as sent (one emoji
is one character). A whitespace-only body is rejected. Mention someone
with `{{mention:N}}` and a `mentions` entry at that index. Names are
filled in by the server. At most 10 mentions, each `accountId` once,
and every entry must appear in the body. A raw `@[Name](accountId)`
token is rejected. A mentioned person who cannot view the discussion
is not notified, and the create still succeeds.

`annotations` is optional, at most 10. `color` is `#RRGGBB`, six hex
digits, either case. `#ffd1dc` is valid. Box coordinates and
dimensions, and pencil points, are fractions of the frame from 0 to 1.
A pencil annotation has 1 to 10 lines, and each line has 2 to 1000
points. On a document or PDF, every box and every pencil line needs a
`pageNumber`.

A timeout can create a duplicate. List the asset's discussions before
retrying.

Returns the discussion with its first comment. `updatedAt` equals
`createdAt` until that comment is edited.

Requires the `comments.write` OAuth scope.

Get one discussion, including its first 10 comments.

A discussion you cannot view is 404, the same as a missing one.
`boardId` is present only when the stored board is active and you can
view it.

Requires the `comments.read` OAuth scope.

Replace a comment's text and mentions.

Only the author can edit. An author who no longer has

changes. An edit that leaves the text and mentions as they are changes
nothing and keeps `updatedAt`. Edits replace mentions and notify no

Omitting `mentions`, or sending `null`, on a comment that has them is
409. Send the mentions again to keep them, or send `mentions: []` to

discussion is 404. Polling the comment list cannot detect the delete.

Requires the `comments.write` OAuth scope.

get.description:
List people in the workspace.

`type` chooses who is included:

- `member` — workspace members. This is the default.
- `guest` — board guests.
- `libraryMember` — people who belong to a library and are not
  workspace members.

`email` without `type` searches every type. `email` with `type`
searches only that type. An unknown email is `{ "data": [], "total": 0 }`,
not 404.

`firstJoinedAt` is the first time that person joined, not the latest.
A member who leaves and rejoins keeps the original value. It is the
stored Postgres timestamp text, not an ISO 8601 string like other
timestamps in this API: a space between date and time, up to 6
fraction digits with trailing zeros dropped, and a UTC offset
(currently `+00`). `2024-03-01 12:00:00.123456+00`,
`2024-03-01 12:00:00.12+00`, and `2024-03-01 12:00:00+00` are all
possible. Don't parse a fixed width.

`id` is the account id. It is the same id as `author.id` on a comment
written by a workspace account, and the same id as `mentions[].id` on
a comment and `mentions[].accountId` when writing one.

Any workspace member can list every type. Board guests and
library-only members cannot call this route.

`members.read` is its own scope. `workspace.read` does not grant it.

ShareLinkSettings.description:
Share link settings you can set. Omitted settings are not changed.

`password`, `expiresAt`, `requireAccount`, `comments` and `customFields` depend on your workspace's plan. Paid plans include them by default, also during the 30-day grace period after a paid plan expires. Turning one on that your plan does not include returns `422` with `type: ADDON_DISABLED`, `extra.addonKey: shareLinks`, and `extra.settings` listing the rejected settings (`password`, `expiration`, `requireAccount`, `comments`, `customFields`). Nothing in the request is applied.

A link keeps the settings it already has, whatever the plan. Sending a value the link already has, changing a password or expiration date the link already has, and turning a setting off always work. Moving `comments` or `customFields` up a level counts as turning it on: from `hidden` to any other value, or from `read_only` to `allowed` or `editable`. Settings a new link takes from your workspace defaults or from a board above it do not count.

active.description: Whether the link works. A disabled link keeps its settings and can be enabled again.

allowDownload.description: Whether visitors can download the original files

password.description: Password visitors must enter to open the link. `null` removes it. Never returned; read `hasPassword` instead.

expiresAt.description: When the link stops working. Must be in the future. `null` removes the expiration.

requireAccount.description: Whether visitors must sign in to Air to open the link

comments.description: What visitors can do with comments. `allowed` lets them add comments, which writes to your workspace.

customFields.description: What visitors can do with custom field values. `editable` lets them change values, which writes to your workspace.

showAllVersions.description: Whether visitors can browse the asset's other versions

url.description: The public CDN URL for the asset or version

followsDefaultVersion.description: When true, the link serves the asset's current default version. When false, the link is pinned to a specific version (`versionId`).

versionId.description: Present when `followsDefaultVersion` is false — the pinned asset version ID

- `PROCESS_TIMED_OUT` - exceeded the maximum amount of time allowed
